service.name: Spanish guitarist
service.serviceType: Solo Spanish guitarist for wedding ceremonies, cocktail hours, dinner parties and corporate dinners
service.description: One Spanish guitarist on nylon strings: Malaguena, rumbas, farrucas and familiar songs played flamenco-style, for wedding ceremonies, cocktail hours, dinner parties, milestone birthdays and corporate dinners across Denver, the Front Range and the Colorado mountain corridor.

faqs.q: What does a Spanish guitarist play?
faqs.a: The pieces people mean when they say Spanish guitar, from a Malaguena to Entre dos Aguas, and familiar songs played in the same style. It's booked through Signet Artists in Denver.

faqs.q: Is a Spanish guitarist the same as flamenco?
faqs.a: It's the solo version of it. Flamenco is an art form of its own, played here by Dirty Flamenco as a trio of guitar, bass and cajon with a set piece in the evening. A Spanish guitarist is one musician on nylon strings doing the quieter job: a ceremony, a cocktail hour, a dinner.

About as loud as a conversation at the next table. Indoors, nylon strings carry a prelude and a processional in most spaces with nothing plugged in at all. Outdoors, or where the officiant needs to be heard at the back, a small sound system on the same stand carries the guitar and a microphone, and the guitarist sets the level to the space.

faqs.q: Who plays a Spanish guitar booking?
faqs.a: A working Spanish guitarist from our roster, and we name them to you when the contract is written. For a particular group by name, ask for Dirty Flamenco, the trio.

faqs.q: Can a Spanish guitarist play a wedding ceremony outdoors?
faqs.a: Yes. The site needs to be covered, level and dry with power run to it, and we agree a plan for moving indoors with you ahead of time.

faqs.q: How much space does one Spanish guitarist need?
faqs.a: A corner of about 6 by 4 feet, with one dedicated 20-amp circuit when the sound system is used, 45 minutes to set up and 30 to pack down.
